title: The Chair: Setting the Tone
summary: The chair's pivotal role in creating the conditions for effective challenge and decision-making, and the behaviours that separate an effective chair from an ineffective one.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The chair's pivotal role in creating the conditions for effective challenge and decision-making, and the behaviours that separate an effective chair from an ineffective one.
Learning Objectives: Explain the chair's responsibilities for board conduct and performance
Assess chairing behaviours that encourage or suppress contribution
Identify how the chair's relationship with the chief executive shapes the board
Syllabus: The chair's role: agenda, discussion, conclusion and board performance
Attributes of an effective chair: authority with humility, patience with incisiveness
Drawing out quieter voices and bringing circular debate to a close
Chair and chief executive: partnership without capture
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members
Executive directors and senior managers who present to or sit on the board
Company secretaries and heads of governance responsible for board processes and evaluation
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No prior governance training is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
Olivier Sibony, You're About to Make a Terrible Mistake! How Biases Distort Decision-Making (2020)
